questions.stem_latex:
A probability distribution is said to have a \textbf{memoryless property} if the probability of some future event occurring is not affected by the occurrence of past events.

In formal statistic terms, a random variable $X$ is said to follow a probability distribution with a memoryless property if for any $a, x \ge 0$ it is true that:

$$P(X > x + a \mid X > a) = P(X > x)$$

You are given that $X$ is modelled by a continuous random variable with probability density function of the form $f(x) = \lambda e^{-\lambda x}$, for some constant $\lambda$.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Show that the corresponding cumulative distribution function is given by $F(x) = 1 - e^{-\lambda x}$.

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
Hence, prove the memoryless property for the distribution of $X$:

$$P(X > x + a \mid X > a) = P(X > x)$$

Method 1: $\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}=\dfrac{T_4}{T_3}$, so $\dfrac{x}{4}=\dfrac{32/27}{y}=\dfrac{32}{27y}$ (1). Also $\dfrac{x}{4}=\dfrac{y}{x}$, so $y=\dfrac{x^2}{4}$ (2).

Substitute (2) into (1): $\dfrac{x}{4}=\dfrac{32}{27\left(\frac{x^2}{4}\right)}=\dfrac{128}{27x^2}$, so $27x^3=512$, $x^3=\dfrac{512}{27}$, $x=\dfrac83$.

When $x=\dfrac83$: $y=\dfrac{(8/3)^2}{4}=\dfrac{64}{36}=\dfrac{16}{9}$.

$\therefore x=\dfrac83$ and $y=\dfrac{16}{9}$.

$y=x^3-x^2-2x$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2-2x-2$.

Set $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$: $3x^2-2x-2=0$, $x=\dfrac{2\pm\sqrt{4+24}}{6}$, so $x\approx1.2$ or $-0.5$.

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=6x-2$.

When $x=1.2$, $y\approx-2.1$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\approx5.2>0$, so a local minimum at $(1.2,-2.1)$.

solutions.latex: $F(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^x\lambda e^{-\lambda t}\,dt=\left[\dfrac{\lambda e^{-\lambda t}}{-\lambda}\right]_0^x=\left[-e^{-\lambda t}\right]_0^x=-e^{-\lambda x}+e^{0}=1-e^{-\lambda x}$

solutions.latex:
$P(X>x+a\mid X>a)=\dfrac{P\left((X>x+a)\cap(X>a)\right)}{P(X>a)}=\dfrac{P(X>x+a)}{P(X>a)}$

$=\dfrac{1-\left(1-e^{-\lambda(x+a)}\right)}{1-\left(1-e^{-\lambda a}\right)}=\dfrac{e^{-\lambda x-\lambda a}}{e^{-\lambda a}}=\dfrac{e^{-\lambda x}\cdot e^{-\lambda a}}{e^{-\lambda a}}=e^{-\lambda x}$

$P(X>x)=1-\left(1-e^{-\lambda x}\right)=e^{-\lambda x}$

$\therefore P(X>x+a\mid X>a)=P(X>x)$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: conditional probability as a ratio; 1: using the cumulative distribution function; 1: simplifying and concluding (must show)
